chapter: Writing, Oklahoma roots and the origins of bebop
title: Writers he learned from: Lunceford, Gerald Wilson, Duke
summary: He admired Lunceford's arrangers and borrowed Duke's muted section voicings.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: By this time, you had gone through several stages in your young career, and you had heard records and had heard arrangements...
...and bands. Who did you like that you might say you picked up on certain things that you could use?
Well, Jimmy Lunceford's band. I liked his band because I liked the way Gerald writes...
Gerald Wilson, yeah. And I liked some of the things that the earlier writers, like...
Sy Oliver and the piano player...
Eddie Wilcox. I liked the way he...
He wrote some things for Lunceford.
Yeah, but I don't know what his material was, because I didn't hear him play an instrument.
So it was Wilcox and Sy Oliver, and then it was Gerald Wilson.

Gerald, yeah. And I copied after them, too, in a sense. I even copied after Duke, with the muted things that he had, with the section playing the mute -- it was a beautiful thing. A lot of bands didn't have that going on in there, so I picked up on a little bit of that. I didn't use much of it, but I mean, I got hip to it, so I knew that I wanted it I could draw back to it -- I could reach out and get that. Which is a great help when you're trying to put something together with all the different sounds and the different...
